name: Hammered Hulls
label: Dischord
lede: The kid on the cover of Minor Threat's first record sings, the guitarist from Helium plays bass, and two DC road dogs fill out a band that may have made the last record ever finished at Inner Ear.

eras.title: Four lifers start over
eras.text: Every member had decades of bands behind them before Dischord dated the group to 2018. Within months the Washington Post was calling it a post-punk supergroup.

years.cap: Mary Timony playing Helium songs at the Independent, San Francisco, February 2018
years.h: Players from Faith, Helium, Medications and Titus Andronicus form a band
years.p: [[Alec MacKaye|bb05a948-ea44-4c9b-9d19-2a48f757ca22]] of [[Faith|f735a867-9a16-451f-8f83-669ed42e2574]] and [[Ignition|3cb2b7d6-1f0b-4ac5-b67f-52132f3d3b61]] sings. [[Mary Timony|d9c8dc3c-15b8-40d5-8153-ae9214aeef55]] of [[Helium|573510d6-bb5d-4d07-b0aa-ea6afe39e28d]] and [[Ex Hex|2f64e1fd-44b3-44f1-a586-b9916966b39f]] plays bass, [[Mark Cisneros|78448563-93ad-4d49-be7f-95bf5fe60021]] of [[Medications|c545a7bf-c8d7-4368-8009-22e19d8911ce]] guitar, and Chris Wilson of [[Titus Andronicus|d38c47f6-d9bb-4a77-aaea-df53a6616a68]] drums.
years.xp: The full résumés run longer. MacKaye also sang in [[The Untouchables|16d88df0-a2a9-4b3b-87ff-84e90e312d40]] and [[The Warmers|af0dea4e-c501-47f2-8695-129f254d425f]]. Timony had fronted Helium and Ex Hex on guitar, so bass was a switch. Cisneros played in [[Deathfix|db0e5c06-c091-46d4-bd42-5ba2ee299123]] and [[Des Demonas|7536e54b-aa8f-429a-aa62-21184a53c14c]] as well, and Wilson drummed for Ted Leo and the Pharmacists before Titus Andronicus.

years.cap: Hammered Hulls on stage at the Black Cat, Washington DC, September 15, 2018
q: Our songs started out punk, straight ahead, super Black Flag.
years.h: The first show comes in September 2018
years.p: Hammered Hulls play live for the first time that September. By December the Washington Post is writing them up as a post-punk supergroup.
years.xp:
The Post piece, headlined as eavesdropping on the new post-punk supergroup, caught a band whose songs were already changing shape. Timony said they'd started out straight-ahead punk and were getting more complicated, more proggy.

MacKaye described the songs as seeming to assemble themselves as the band worked.

eras.title: A 7" in a single day
eras.text: The band went into Inner Ear with Don Zientara and Ian MacKaye, the studio Dischord has leaned on since the early '80s, and had three songs done in a day. The 7" put them on Dischord and on the road.

years.h: Three songs, one day, Ian MacKaye at the board
years.p: Written Words, Self Inflicted and Looking After You are recorded at Inner Ear Studios with [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]] and [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]], Alec's older brother. It comes out as Hammered Hulls, Dischord No. 188.
years.xp: Stereogum premiered Written Words on July 16. Asked about the band's name, Alec MacKaye feverishly built an explanation on the spot. The 7" came on mixed-color vinyl, with East Coast shows to follow.

years.cap: Alec MacKaye singing at the Black Cat Backstage, Washington DC, December 19, 2018
years.h: Baltimore on August 28, New York the night after
years.p: The 7" goes on the road: Baltimore on August 28, New York on August 29.

eras.title: The last record at Inner Ear
eras.text: The album was started before the pandemic shut everything down and finished in the second half of 2021. Dischord says it may be the last record recorded and mixed at Inner Ear, the studio behind most of the label's history.

years.h: Careening gets finished at Inner Ear, maybe for the last time
years.p: Begun just before the pandemic lockdown, the album is finished there in summer and fall 2021, engineered by Don Zientara and produced by Ian MacKaye.
years.xp:
Dischord says Careening may be the last record made at the studio. Inner Ear, Zientara's place, had recorded Dischord bands since the label's earliest days, and for the Hulls the sessions bridged the whole pandemic.

Dischord describes the result as vulnerable songs, only barely contained, with strong contributions from each member.

years.p: The debut album runs twelve songs, from Boilermaker's Notch and Bog People to Mission Statement. Dischord No. 193.
years.xp: Brooklyn Vegan and Stereogum premiered Rights and Reproduction ahead of release. Written Word returned from the 2019 7", and shows followed through the fall and winter.

yt: Hardest Road, Third Man Records, Detroit, 2026
years.h: The blue-vinyl Careening and a band still on the road
years.p: According to Discogs, the LP goes back to press on blue vinyl. Dischord's band page lists the band as active and on tour.
